newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 27.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 27. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Former Interior Minister Rudini has called for candidates for the office of president and vice-president to be announced during the general election campaign period starting next month rather than wait as in the past for a special session of parliament scheduled for March next year.
Indonesia's military have denied there were any fatalities during a protest in East Timor on Sunday during the visit of a special envoy of the U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
A local consortium PT Kresna Kusuma Dyandra Marga has secured a two trillion rupiah ($847 million) syndicated loan to build a 21.5 km (13 miles) toll road linking Jakarta and Bekasi in West Java.
Minister for Toursim, Post and Telecommunications Joop Ave has said Telkom's monopoly on local and domestic long distance calls will not be shortened.
Seventeen people have been detained after rioting in the Central Java town of Pekalongan which was triggered by unhappiness from local people over a concert by a politically aligned popular singer.

Indonesia's mines and energy ministry has formed a special team to investigate reports that the size of the Busang gold find in Kalimantan has been overstated by the Canadian mining company which found it.
